title: Pressure and Cross-Flow Dependent Interfacial Fouling of Mesoporous PES-PUMA Membranes during Water-in-Oil Emulsion Separation
content: Water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion treatment is challenging because efficient membrane separation requires simultaneous control of oil transport, water rejection, interfacial interactions, and fouling resistance. However, the coupled effects of operating pressure and cross-flow hydrodynamics on membrane pore accessibility, foulant-layer evolution, and the permeability-rejection trade-off during cyclic W/O emulsion treatment remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a novel electrospun mesoporous polyurethane-melamine/polyethersulfone (PES-PUMA) membrane was evaluated for the separation of stabilized W/O emulsions under different operating pressures and feed flow rates. At an ultra-low pressure of 20 kPa, the membrane achieved an oil permeate flux of 36.5 ± 2.7 L m⁻² h⁻¹ and a water rejection of 93.1 ± 2.1%. Increasing the operating pressure to 100 kPa increased the oil permeate flux to 87.6 ± 3.5 L m⁻² h⁻¹, while decreasing water rejection to 78.2 ± 1.8%. Increasing the cross-flow from 0.05 to 0.5 mL s-1 increased the oil permeate flux from 23.4 ± 0.7 to 90.7 ± 2.1 L m⁻² h⁻¹, while decreasing water rejection from 95.3 ± 2.1% to 78.4 ± 1.2%. Although higher cross-flow reduced foulant-layer thickness and favored more reversible fouling, increasing operating pressure promoted pore constriction and compact foulant deposition. These findings establish a direct pressure-cross-flow-structure-fouling relationship, showing that hydraulic operating conditions regulate membrane transport pathways and fouling reversibility. This study provides a mechanistic insight into the interfacial and fouling behavior of mesoporous PES-PUMA membranes and establishes a basis for balancing permeability, water rejection, and fouling resistance during W/O emulsion separation.
